items.title: Section: Fulfilling-Requests and Both-Worlds-Happiness Diligence — Handled by a Single Elegant Cross-Reference

items.zh: 菩薩所有遂求精進、此世他世樂精進，如忍應知。其差別者，彼說堪忍，此說菩薩精進勇悍。
items.en: A bodhisattva's fulfilling-requests diligence and diligence of happiness in this world and the next should be understood exactly as described in the chapter on patience. The only difference is this: that chapter spoke of enduring, while here it is spoken of as a bodhisattva's own courageous, resolute diligence.

items.title: Section: Purity Diligence Opens — Matched Antidotes, Genuine Habituation, No Delay, and Correctly Received Teaching

items.zh: 云何菩薩清淨精進？謂此精進略有十種。一、相稱精進，二、串習精進，三、無緩精進，四、善攝精進，五、應時修習精進，六、通達眾相精進，七、不退弱精進，八、不捨軛精進，九、平等精進，十、迴向大菩提精進。若諸菩薩，或為彼彼諸隨煩惱極所逼切，為斷彼彼隨煩惱故，修習種種相稱對治。謂為對治諸貪欲故，修習不淨；為欲對治諸瞋恚故，修習慈愍；為欲對治諸愚癡故，修習觀察緣性緣起；為欲對治諸尋思故，修習息念；為欲對治諸憍慢故，修界差別。如是等類，是名菩薩相稱精進。若諸菩薩，非唯成就始業、初業所有精進；謂為住心教授教誡，非不亦由串習加行、積習加行。是名菩薩串習精進。若諸菩薩，亦非唯有串習加行、積習加行，為住其心教授教誡；然此始業、初業菩薩，於此加行不緩加行、無間加行、殷重加行。是名菩薩無緩精進。若諸菩薩從師長所，或自多聞力所持故，無倒而取，為住其心發勤精進。是名菩薩善攝精進。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's purity diligence? This diligence is, in brief, of ten kinds. First, matched diligence: to counter craving, cultivating contemplation of impurity; to counter aversion, cultivating loving-kindness; to counter confusion, cultivating the contemplation of dependent origination; to counter restless discursive thought, cultivating mindfulness of the breath; to counter pride, cultivating the elemental composition of the body. All such practice is called a bodhisattva's matched diligence. Bodhisattvas whose diligence is never limited to what a genuine beginner first accomplishes, with respect to the instruction received for settling the mind, but who apply themselves through genuine, sustained habituation and accumulated practice — this is called a bodhisattva's habituation diligence. Bodhisattvas whose diligence goes beyond habituation and accumulated practice alone, applying, as genuine beginners, this practice without delay, without interruption, and with real thoroughness — this is called a bodhisattva's diligence without delay. Bodhisattvas who, from a genuine teacher, or through the strength of their own extensive learning, receive the correct method without any distortion, and diligently apply themselves to settling the mind accordingly — this is called a bodhisattva's well-received diligence.

items.title: Section: Timely Practice, Mastering Every Meditative Sign, and Never Settling for Partial Attainment

items.zh: 若諸菩薩無倒取已，於應止時，能正修止；於應舉時，能策其心；於應捨時，能正修捨。是名菩薩應時修習相應精進。若諸菩薩於其種種止、舉、捨相，入、住、出相，能善了知、能無忘失、能善通達，無間修作、殷重修作。是名菩薩通達眾相相應精進。若諸菩薩聞說種種最極廣大、最極甚深、不可思議、不可度量菩薩精進，不自輕蔑，心不怯弱，不於所有少分下劣差別證中而生喜足，不求上進。是名菩薩不退弱精進。若諸菩薩，於時時間密護根門、飲食知量、初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽、正知而住。於如是類等持資糧能攝受轉，即於其中熾然修習，於能引攝無倒義利，於一切時勤加功用。是名菩薩不捨軛精進。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, having received the method correctly, correctly cultivate calming when calming is called for, rouse and steady the mind when rousing is called for, and correctly cultivate equanimity when equanimity is called for — this is called a bodhisattva's timely diligence. Bodhisattvas who thoroughly understand, never forget, and thoroughly penetrate the various signs of calming, rousing, and equanimity, and of entering, abiding in, and emerging from absorption, applying themselves without interruption and with real thoroughness — this is called a bodhisattva's diligence mastering every sign. Bodhisattvas who, hearing described the vast, profound, inconceivable, immeasurable scope of a bodhisattva's own diligence, do not belittle themselves, whose minds do not grow faint-hearted, and who do not mistake any partial or inferior attainment for genuine completion, never ceasing to seek further progress — this is called a bodhisattva's diligence that never weakens. Bodhisattvas who, time after time, carefully guard the sense-doors, eat with genuine moderation, diligently practice the yoga of wakefulness through the first and last watches of the night, and abide with clear awareness — sustaining these supports for meditative stability, applying themselves to them with real intensity, diligently applying effort at every time towards what genuinely and correctly brings real benefit — this is called a bodhisattva's diligence that never sets down the yoke.

items.title: Section: Balanced Union of Calm and Insight, Dedication to Supreme Awakening — the Entire Perfection of Diligence, and Fascicle 42, Reach Their Close

items.zh: 若諸菩薩發勤精進、不緩不急、平等雙運；普於一切應作事中，亦能平等殷重修作。是名菩薩平等精進。若諸菩薩一切精進有所為作，無不皆為迴向無上正等菩提。是名菩薩迴向大菩提精進。如是最初自性精進，乃至最後清淨精進，皆得菩薩大菩提果。菩薩依此所有精進，圓滿精進波羅蜜多，能於無上正等菩提速疾已證、當證、今證。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who apply diligent effort neither too slack nor too forced, calming and insight genuinely joined and operating together, and who, across every work to be accomplished through the spiritual powers, likewise sustain this same balanced, thorough application — this is called a bodhisattva's balanced diligence. Bodhisattvas for whom every single instance of diligent effort, whatever its specific undertaking, is invariably dedicated towards supreme, complete awakening — this is called a bodhisattva's diligence dedicated to supreme awakening. In this way, diligence from its very first intrinsic nature through to this final purity diligence altogether brings about a bodhisattva's great fruit of awakening. Relying on all of this diligence, bodhisattvas fulfil the perfection of diligence, and are able to swiftly realise supreme, complete awakening — whether already realised, soon to be realised, or being realised even now.

blocks.text: The last aspects of diligence, closing fascicle 42.
Diligence that fulfils requests and brings joy now and later is "exactly as described in the chapter on patience. The only difference: that chapter spoke of enduring; this one of striving."

Matched to the affliction: "to counter craving, impurity; to counter aversion, loving-kindness; to counter confusion, dependent origination", and so on (Day 225). Habituated; without delay; correctly received teaching. Venerable Miào Jìng: free of conceit and scatteredness.

"Calming when calming is called for, rousing when rousing is called for, letting be with equanimity when that is called for" (Day 269); mastering every meditative sign; never settling for partial attainment.

"Neither too slack nor too forced, calm and insight joined and operating together", across "all that should be done" (Venerable Miào Jìng: such as supernormal powers), "dedicated to supreme awakening". Master Cháng Bǎi: the *Yújiā lùnjì* calls this "inexhaustible diligence": the bodhisattva's overall direction.
Discipline completed, patience, and diligence: three perfections in one fascicle. Fascicle 43 covers the perfections of meditative concentration and wisdom.

quiz.q: How does the treatise explain fulfilling-requests and two-world diligence?
options: understood as in the patience chapter — there enduring, here courageous diligence
quiz.why: "Should be understood exactly as described in the chapter on patience. The only difference: that chapter spoke of enduring, while here it is spoken of as courageous diligence." Master Cháng Bǎi: replace the patience chapter's wording with diligence and it is the same.

quiz.q: In matched diligence, "to counter conceit and pride, cultivate analysis of the elements" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish "jiāo" and "màn"?
options: jiāo is self-inflation; màn is looking down on others
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "jiāo" is puffing oneself up; "màn" is looking down on others; "discursive thought" means scatteredness. Master Cháng Bǎi: the analysis of the six elements — earth, water, fire, wind, space, consciousness.

quiz.q: In matched diligence, what is cultivated to counter craving, aversion, and confusion respectively?
options: contemplation of impurity, loving-kindness, and dependent origination
quiz.why: "To counter craving, cultivating contemplation of impurity; to counter aversion, loving-kindness; to counter confusion, the contemplation of dependent origination." Venerable Miào Jìng: if your greed is strong and you practise loving-kindness instead — trouble; the object must match the affliction.

quiz.q: Balanced diligence "in all things to be done" is rendered "across everything they undertake." How do the lectures explain "all things to be done"?
options: Miào Jìng: "all things to be done" refers to supernormal accomplishments, when calm and insight are joined at the noble path; Cháng Bǎi cites the eight liberations, eight masteries, ten totalities
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "all that should be done" here refers to supernormal powers. Master Cháng Bǎi: such as the eight liberations, eight masteries, and ten totalities. The English generalises it to everything undertaken.

quiz.q: The last purity diligence, "dedicated to great awakening" — what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the 《瑜伽論記》 calls it?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the 《瑜伽論記》 calls this "inexhaustible diligence" — the bodhisattva's overall aim and direction. Venerable Miào Jìng: past bodhisattvas have realised it, future ones will, present ones are realising it now.
